Summary
I build and run my own LLM inference stack on local hardware, and I use it to ship sourcing tools: market mapping that surfaces the talent pools a title search never returns, and candidate reads where every claim traces back to the person's own words. The tools run on my hardware, so candidate data never goes to a third party model.

Underneath that is a decade of technical recruiting. Engineering leadership, AI/ML, cloud, autonomous vehicles, aerospace, healthcare and executive search, for hypergrowth startups, Fortune-scale platforms and mission-driven organizations. Intake and market calibration through sourcing, screening, interview management, offer negotiation and close.

What I am actually good at is finding people whose experience does not map cleanly to the job title. I staffed autonomous-vehicle simulation out of Rockstar, Pixar and Blue Origin. I placed the Mission Operations Flight Director for MethaneSAT. I cut time-to-hire 13% and time-to-fill 20% at Cruise, and raised hiring-manager acceptance 44% at Tillster.

Before recruiting I spent over a decade in narrative, editorial, documentary and brand storytelling. That is not a detour. It is why I can tell you what is worth saying to a candidate, and why I do not let the machine say it.
